endorsements.quote: To address this, the dataset should be divided into a training set (typically 70%-80%), on which the model is developed, and a test set (20%-30%), which is kept completely separate and used only for final evaluation.
Reporting area under the curve (AUC) alone is no longer sufficient for publication.

The TRIPOD-AI checklist should be completed prior to submission, as commonly omitted items include calibration reporting, specification of the train-test split with a random seed, classification threshold selection, and subgroup performance analysis.
A practical approach is to evaluate model performance separately across key subgroups and report any disparities transparently and prominently.
In many jurisdictions, clinical decision support tools may require additional regulatory review and can be classified as medical devices [ 26 ].
Any study using patient data, whether retrospective or de-identified, requires Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval or clearance from an equivalent ethics committee prior to use for research.

unlisted_practices: Test multiple candidate model algorithms and select the one with the best performance on the available data.
Use k-fold cross-validation instead of a single train-test split for small datasets.
Include both internal cross-validation and an independent external validation cohort from a different institution in published prediction models.
Explicitly acknowledge limitations of single-center retrospective AI studies, including selection bias, limited generalizability, lack of external validation, overfitting and algorithmic bias risk.
Consider logistic regression as the first-line approach when the dataset is small, the outcome is binary or maximum interpretability is required.
Involve clinicians in AI model development so that clinical context guides which outcomes are predicted and for which populations.
Prioritize validation, monitoring, and safe integration into clinical practice as prediction tools move toward deployment.
Clinicians deploying AI tools should remain informed of applicable regulatory requirements.

screen.reason: The article is a practical guide, framework, and commentary outlining steps for clinicians to develop and deploy predictive AI tools rather than an empirical evaluation of a clinical AI tool or deployment practice.
